mathgap.title: Signed 'has N more than'
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'X has N more than Y', interpret it as the signed equation X = Y + N (or X - Y = N). Do not assume N is positive.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a 'has N more than' clause appears.
mathgap.example: Treating 'X has 5 more than Y' as X = |Y| + 5, ignoring sign.

mathgap.title: Signed relational equation
mathgap.principle: For statements like 'The number of X that A has more than B is equal to the difference between the number of X that C and D have', translate to (A - B) = (C - D) using signed subtraction.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a relational equality involving 'more than' and 'difference between' appears.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'A has more than B equals difference between C and D' as |A - B| = |C - D|.

mathgap.title: Allow negative differences
mathgap.principle: Do not assume that a difference or 'more than' clause guarantees a positive result; keep the sign as written.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a difference or 'more than' relationship could be negative.
mathgap.example: Assuming 'A has 3 more than B' forces A > B even when other equations imply otherwise.

mathgap.title: Model transfers as net changes
mathgap.principle: Each statement 'X gives N to Y' reduces X's count by N and increases Y's count by N. Apply all such transfers as net changes to the variables.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'X gives N to Y' as X gains N and Y loses N.

mathgap.title: Initial count statements
mathgap.principle: Plain statements like 'X has N' describe the initial amount before any transfers or other operations. Use them as starting values.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering a direct count statement without qualifiers.
mathgap.example: Treating 'X has N' as the final count after all other actions have occurred.

mathgap.title: Systematic equation solving
mathgap.principle: Represent each person as a variable, write a linear equation for every relational statement and every transfer, then solve the resulting linear system.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After translating all statements into equations.
mathgap.example: Skipping the creation of equations and guessing values directly.

mathgap.title: Distinct variables for similar names
mathgap.principle: Treat each distinct name as a separate variable, even if the names are similar (e.g., Orval vs Orvil).
mathgap.when_to_apply: When parsing the list of participants.
mathgap.example: Merging 'Alberta' and 'Albert' into a single variable.

mathgap.title: Target-focused statement selection
mathgap.principle: When solving a mathgap problem, first identify all statements that involve the person whose count is being asked, and ignore statements that do not mention that person, as they are irrelevant to the final answer.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Immediately after reading the problem, before setting up equations.
mathgap.example: Attempting to solve the entire system of equations even though only a few statements involve the target person, leading to unnecessary complexity and errors.

mathgap.title: Combined sum interpretation
mathgap.principle: For statements like 'X has N more than Y and Z combined', translate to the signed equation X = Y + Z + N (or equivalently X - (Y + Z) = N).
mathgap.when_to_apply: When parsing relational statements that mention 'combined' or a sum of multiple people.
mathgap.example: Treating 'X has N more than Y and Z combined' as X = Y + N (ignoring Z) or as X = Y + Z - N, which yields an incorrect equation.

mathgap.title: Increase by factor interpretation
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'the number of X increases by N times', interpret it as a multiplication: new amount = old amount * N.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'the number of potatoes that X has increases by 2 times' as X_new = X_old + 2, instead of X_new = X_old * 2.

mathgap.description: Using absolute value for 'difference between' clauses
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats the phrase 'difference between' as an unsigned distance, ignoring the sign, which loses directionality in equations.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret 'difference between A and B' as signed subtraction A - B, preserving sign.

mathgap.description: Assuming positivity for 'has more than' statements
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes that 'X has N more than Y' implies X > Y, overlooking that N could be negative or that the relationship might be part of a contradictory system.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat 'has N more than' as a signed equation X = Y + N without assuming N is positive.

mathgap.description: Treating 'X has N' as a final count after transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model interprets initial count statements as describing the final state, missing the effect of subsequent transfers or operations.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Consider 'X has N' as the initial amount before any transfers or other operations, and apply subsequent changes accordingly.

mathgap.description: Applying transfers in the wrong direction
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model reverses the giver and receiver when interpreting 'X gives N to Y', subtracting from Y and adding to X.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When parsing 'X gives N to Y', subtract N from X and add N to Y.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting 'increase by X times' as addition rather than multiplication
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model reads 'increase by N times' as adding N to the current amount, instead of scaling the amount by a factor.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret 'increase by N times' as multiplying the current amount by N (new = old * N).
